newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US agree maximum effort for stable forex-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US agree maximum effort for stable forex-MOF.

text.p: Japan and the United States have agreed that they will make maximum efforts to stabilise currency markets, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.
"Japan and the United States have agreed to tackle the issue of stability in currency markets with maximum attention," Mitsuzuka told the committee.
He said Japan had told the Group of Seven (G7) nations at last Sunday's meeting in Washington that stable currency markets were positive for continued growth without inflation.
He also said Japan's economic recovery was becoming firmer from being gradual.
He said Japan was putting efforts into structural reform of its economy and strengthening the credibility of its financial system.

Mitsuzuka added that the G7 finance ministers and central bankers agreed at their Washington meeting that it was not favourable for currencies to deviate substantially from economic fundamentals, and they should avoid currency rates which would lead to trade imbalances. These points were all included in the communique issued at the meeting, he said.
